references.text: The three hundred men blew their trumpets together, which led to the confusion described in verse 22.
Similar divine intervention where enemies turned their swords against each other in confusion during Jonathan's attack on the Philistines.
The Lord caused the enemies to fight against each other when Jehoshaphat and Judah met the Moabites and Ammonites.
The prophecy that the Lord will set Egyptians against Egyptians, so they shall fight one another—the same principle of divine confusion among enemies.
The prophecy that the Lord will send confusion among the enemies so that they seize each other's hands and lift their hand against one another.
The Lord brings forth a sword against Gog, and every man's sword shall be against his brother—the same motif of divine confusion.
The Lord brought confusion over the Egyptian army at the Red Sea, a similar example of divine intervention in battle.
